title: Anorexia nervosa: low body weight is the key discriminator
vignette: A 20-year-old college student comes to the office due to fatigue and decreased exercise tolerance. She says, "I used to run 5 miles every day, but for the past month I get out of breath after running 3 miles. I need to keep running so I don't get any fatter than I already am." The patient also reports difficulty concentrating in class, depressed mood, constipation, and abdominal bloating. Her appetite is normal, but she admits to occasionally forcing herself to vomit to prevent weight gain. Physical examination is significant for dry skin, painless bilateral parotid swelling, pharyngeal erythema, and hypoactive bowel sounds. Temperature is 36.2 C (97.2 F), blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg, pulse is 62/min, and respirations are 16/min. BMI is 17.5 kg/m2. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

clues.text: I don't get any fatter than I already am
clues.note: A distorted body image and intense fear of weight gain despite being underweight are core features of anorexia nervosa. (Sensitive topic - handled clinically.)

clues.text: forcing herself to vomit to prevent weight gain
clues.note: Self-induced vomiting (with parotid swelling, pharyngeal erythema) indicates the binge-eating/purging SUBTYPE of anorexia nervosa - present when body weight is significantly low.
A significantly LOW body weight (BMI 17.5, below 18.5) is the KEY feature distinguishing anorexia nervosa from bulimia nervosa (in which weight is normal or above).

whatMatters: Significantly LOW body weight (BMI 17.5) + intense fear of weight gain + distorted body image = ANOREXIA NERVOSA. Purging (vomiting) here reflects the binge-eating/purging SUBTYPE of anorexia - the low body weight is what distinguishes it from bulimia nervosa (normal/high weight). Answer A.
strategy: Use body weight to separate anorexia from bulimia: anorexia nervosa = significantly LOW weight (with fear of gaining/distorted image), which may be restricting or binge/purge subtype; bulimia nervosa = binge + compensatory behavior at NORMAL or above weight. Her BMI 17.5 -> anorexia. Reject bulimia (weight low here), body dysmorphic disorder (preoccupation with a perceived appearance defect, not weight/eating), hypothyroidism (would not explain low weight/purging), irritable bowel syndrome (no eating-disorder features), and major depression (mood symptoms here are from malnutrition).

eliminations.label: Body dysmorphic disorder - perceived appearance defect (not weight)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: preoccupation with a perceived or slight defect in physical appearance. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is not diagnosed when the body-image distortion is part of an eating disorder with low weight and fear of weight gain. ✅ Correct if: distress over a specific perceived flaw (e.g., nose/skin) without an eating disorder.

eliminations.label: Bulimia nervosa - normal/above weight (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: recurrent binge eating with compensatory behavior (vomiting, laxatives, exercise) at a NORMAL or increased body weight. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: this patient's weight is significantly LOW (BMI 17.5), which places purging behavior within the anorexia binge/purge subtype, not bulimia. ✅ Correct if: binge/purge with normal-to-high body weight.

eliminations.label: Hypothyroidism - wouldn't explain low weight/purging
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: hypothyroidism (fatigue, constipation, cold intolerance). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it typically causes weight GAIN and doesn't explain fear of weight gain, distorted body image, or self-induced vomiting. ✅ Correct if: fatigue/constipation with weight gain and low free T4/high TSH.

eliminations.label: Irritable bowel syndrome - no eating-disorder features
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: chronic abdominal pain with altered bowel habits and bloating. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it doesn't explain purging, distorted body image, or significantly low weight. ✅ Correct if: chronic abdominal pain + altered bowel habits without an eating disorder.

eliminations.label: Major depressive disorder - mood symptoms from malnutrition
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a mood disorder with depressed mood, poor concentration, fatigue. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: she doesn't meet full criteria, and her depressed mood/fatigue/poor concentration are consistent with the effects of malnutrition, not a primary depression. ✅ Correct if: full depressive syndrome without the eating-disorder core features.

reasoning: Significantly low body weight (BMI 17.5) + intense fear of weight gain + distorted body image = anorexia nervosa
Self-induced vomiting indicates the binge-eating/purging SUBTYPE of anorexia
Low body weight distinguishes anorexia from bulimia (which occurs at normal/high weight)
mechanism: Anorexia nervosa is defined by (1) significantly LOW body weight relative to age/height (BMI <=18.5 in adults), (2) an intense FEAR of gaining weight or persistent behavior that interferes with weight gain, and (3) a DISTORTED body image / undue influence of weight on self-worth. There are two subtypes: RESTRICTING (limiting intake, excessive exercise, no regular purging) and BINGE-EATING/PURGING (regular vomiting, laxatives, or diuretics). This patient's low BMI (17.5), fear of getting 'fatter,' compulsive exercise, and self-induced vomiting place her in the binge/purge subtype of anorexia. Physical/metabolic sequelae include emaciation, bradycardia, hypotension, hypothermia, dry skin, lanugo, amenorrhea, and, with vomiting, PAROTID hypertrophy, pharyngeal erythema, dental erosions, and hypokalemia/metabolic alkalosis; her depressed mood, fatigue, and poor concentration reflect malnutrition. The KEY feature distinguishing anorexia from BULIMIA nervosa is the abnormally LOW body weight - bulimia involves binge/purge cycles at a NORMAL or above-normal weight. (Sensitive topic: eating disorders are serious and treatable; support resources such as the National Alliance for Eating Disorders helpline are appropriate - I can help find them if useful.)

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Psych > anorexia nervosa: low body weight, fear of weight gain, distorted body image; restricting vs binge/purge subtypes; bradycardia, amenorrhea, parotid hypertrophy (purging); key vs bulimia = low weight.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Purging can occur in anorexia; the LOW body weight (BMI 17.5) makes it anorexia, not bulimia.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on anorexia vs bulimia, binge/purge subtype, distorted body image, or BMI cutoffs? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Bulimia = normal/high weight; body dysmorphic = perceived defect; hypothyroidism = weight gain; IBS/depression lack eating-disorder core.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: anorexia = LOW body weight + fear of weight gain + distorted image (restricting or binge/purge); bulimia = normal weight. Sensitive - resources available.

memoryHook: Purging can happen in either disorder - the scale decides: a BMI of 17.5 means anorexia (binge/purge subtype), because bulimia keeps a normal weight.
